questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Do NOT try uniplaces, I ended up renting a very bad place and had to find a new one. I found the new place through a contact in Portugal.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: DO NOT use uniplaces for accommodation, try local websites, maybe your contact person from receiving university can help you with this. Or try to contact campus directly through mail.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: My institution did not offer much unfortunately, but I was able to make my own friends while there. They offered me a student contact person who helped a bit, but I never met him...

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Meet som locals, and through them you can get even more friends. Go and explore the city you live in, eat good food and enjoy concerts and museums.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities! It's cheap with bus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be very open and curious. Show interest in their language and culture and they will love you! Portuguese people are very nice and easy going, so it was not hard.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the language. They are very laid back and everything is at an later hour than in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmth, easy to talk with people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Get everything in order before going. My arrangements were spontaneous and quite last minute - at my own fault, which had its own consequences. 
2) The non-academic activities is as important as the academic, so prioritize this!
3) Do not expect everything to be the same standard as UCPH.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: the best thing would be if you know any locals before hand, who can help you with accomodation if you live off campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The non academic part!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be on your own and be the only one who can solve your problems. Starting from scratch, knowing very few people and building your own social circles. Don't give up during hard times. And make sure to go out of the "international bobble" and get to know the locals!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Going on exchange is such an important part of academia I think. You get to have a unique perspective on things and you get to meet people who are very different from you and yet similar in other aspects.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
